claims.locator: Chapter2 p15 Eq2.1 and following explanation
claims.proposed_status: Established by ordinary exact analysis; narrow mathematical target fully addressed.
claims.argument: For any finite real beta0,beta1 and genetic value g, exp(beta0+beta1*g)>0. If g is a finite-variance Gaussian variable it is finite almost surely, so the environmental variance is strictly positive almost surely.
limits: This concerns variance, not standard deviation; it does not establish empirical fit or any bias-removal claim.
Finite-precision overflow or underflow is a separate implementation issue, not a counterexample to positivity over real numbers.
claims.remaining: No substantive algebraic gap; Lean absence is only a separate formal-certification limitation.

claims.locator: Chapter2 p21 Eq2.16; environmental variance definition p15 Eq2.1
claims.proposed_status: Established by ordinary exact analysis with positive genetic variance; numerical illustration and empirical power are separate.
claims.argument: Let V_A>0 denote the genetic variance, s_A=sqrt(V_A), and v_E(g)=exp(beta0+beta1*g). Then v_E(g+s_A)/v_E(g)=exp(beta1*s_A)=Delta>0 for any g. Taking logarithms uniquely gives beta1=log(Delta)/s_A. In particular the source comparison uses g=0 and g=s_A; its baseline environmental variance is exp(beta0), not beta0 itself.
claims.existing_evidence: outputs/analytic-checks.json delta values evaluate the inverse at V_A=0.5 for Delta1,1.3,1.5,1.7. Those evaluations corroborate but are not needed for the exact identity.
limits: For V_A=0, Delta=1 for any finite beta1 and the inverse formula divides by zero; beta1 is not identified by this ratio.
This is an environmental-VARIANCE ratio. The environmental-SD ratio for the same genetic shift is sqrt(Delta).

The adjacent source example for Delta1.5 writes 0.5*1.5=0.75, while the preceding example uses environmental baseline0.2. The general identity does not validate a common-baseline reading of those numerical examples; that arithmetic/source-context discrepancy is a separate target.
claims.remaining: No outstanding mathematical obligation for the stated identity under V_A>0,Delta>0; simulation recovery/power remains separate.

claims.locator: Chapter3 p36 Eq3.3 and p37 Eqs3.4-3.6; inspected evidence/eq3-information.png
claims.proposed_status: Analytical audit completed with a literal formula discrepancy: Eq3.4 is correct for unit slope, but not for general source OPLM slopes. Additivity and inverse-information uncertainty require their stated interpretation.
argument: For Y~Bernoulli(p(theta)), p=logistic(a*(theta-b)), the theta score is a*(Y-p). Thus Fisher information for theta is E[score^2]=a^2*p*(1-p), also equal to minus expected second derivative.

The crop confirms Eq3.4 actually prints p*(1-p), without a^2. At a=2,theta=b, true theta information is1, whereas the printed expression is1/4. Existing finite-difference output 0.9999999999131821 independently corroborates this exact discrepancy.

For unit positive slope a=1, Eq3.4 is correct. It also equals information for each item-specific logit coordinate eta=a*(theta-b), but those differently scaled coordinates cannot be treated as a single common theta without Jacobian factors.

Under fixed known calibration and conditional item independence, the likelihood factors and the total theta score is the sum of independent mean-zero item scores. Its variance equals the sum of the correct item information values, establishing Eq3.5.

TI(theta)^(-1/2) is the conventional information-based conditional standard-error function for TI>0. If interpreted as an exact finite-sample sampling SD or an arbitrary posterior SD, Eq3.6 is not generally established: equality with actual estimator variance requires efficiency/appropriate approximation, and posterior uncertainty depends on the prior.
limits: No missing discrimination factor can be excused merely because the OPLM slopes are treated as known; their derivatives with respect to theta still enter information.
Actual Figure3.2 computations/calibration files were not obtained. A printed error does not establish that its plotted implementation omitted a^2.
Information additivity and normalization of SE cannot validate the source empirical biometric conclusions.
claims.remaining: Actual plotted implementation remains unresolved; no additional algebra or model run is needed to establish the printed unit-slope versus OPLM distinction.

claims.locator: Chapter4 p56 Eqs4.6-4.10; AppendixB pp134-136 lines34-39,44-49,80-85,90-96; inspected evidence/eq4-probabilities.png
claims.proposed_status: Normalized AppendixB probability/adjacent-logit target established by ordinary algebra. Literal printed equations fail normalization; do not collapse these two verdicts.
argument: AppendixB defines eta_k=alpha*(theta-beta_k), s_k=sum_{l=1}^k eta_l, and p_k=exp(s_k)/sum_{j=1}^3 exp(s_j). For finite real inputs each term is positive, the denominator is positive, and sum_k p_k=1 exactly.

For k=2,3, log(p_k/p_{k-1})=s_k-s_{k-1}=alpha*(theta-beta_k). Thus adjacent-category logits agree with the implemented cumulative-exponential model. The common eta_1 factor cancels from all probabilities: after cancellation weights are 1, exp(eta_2), exp(eta_2+eta_3). beta_1 fixed at0 is a redundant reference contribution, with effective transitions at beta_2,beta_3.

The inspected crop instead prints p_no=1/(1+u*v), p_question=p_no*u, p_yes=p_no*p_question*v, with u=exp(alpha*(theta-beta_1)), v=exp(alpha*(theta-beta_2)). At theta=0 and both displayed thresholds0, alpha=1, these probabilities are1/2,1/2,1/4, summing to5/4. The discrepancy is in the source ink, not merely text extraction.

At that zero setting, the AppendixB cumulative-exponential model gives three probabilities1/3. Its indexing uses beta_2,beta_3 as transitions; one cannot silently identify these with the literal printed beta_1,beta_2 expressions without explaining the remapping.
claims.existing_evidence: outputs/analytic-checks.json ch4_probability_check and simulation/analytic_checks.py already retain this zero-setting counterexample separately from AppendixB probabilities. The present derivation checks normalization and adjacent ratios for all finite real inputs, beyond that one numerical setting.
limits: This certifies the mathematical probability kernel specified by the printed AppendixB code, not that empirical fits ran that exact source version or converged.
Floating-point exponentials can overflow; the ordinary real-arithmetic identity is not a numerical-stability certification.
The normalized implementation must not be described as faithful reproduction of Eqs4.6-4.9 as literally printed.
claims.remaining: No substantive algebraic gap for implemented normalization/adjacent logits. Empirical implementation provenance, fitted results and unrelated posterior uncertainty remain separate.

formalization: No Lean formalization is supplied. That does not make these completed ordinary analytical checks unattempted; any formal-certification publication gate remains separate.
scope: Proposed guidance only; principal empirical claims are not adjudicated by these narrow analytical findings.
